entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Coptic Orthodox Church of Alexandria is one of the world's oldest Christian churches — claiming founding by the Evangelist Mark in Alexandria, Egypt in approximately 42 CE — and represents the largest Christian community in the Middle East (approximately 10-15 million Copts, roughly 10% of Egypt's population) as well as a worldwide diaspora, maintaining one of the most ancient and unbroken Christian traditions in the world across nearly two millennia of continuous worship in Egypt.

Coptic Christianity is extraordinarily ancient: the Coptic language (a descendant of ancient Egyptian, written in a Greek-derived alphabet) is still used in Coptic liturgy — representing one of the world's most ancient languages in continuous religious use, a direct link to ancient Egyptian civilization that predates the Arab conquest of Egypt (641 CE). Coptic art and iconography have distinctive ancient Egyptian aesthetic influences visible in icon painting styles, representing a unique synthesis of ancient Egyptian, Hellenistic, and Christian traditions.

The Coptic community has faced severe persecution: the Roman persecutions (particularly Diocletian's Great Persecution of 303-311 CE — still commemorated in the Coptic calendar beginning from 284 CE as the 'Era of Martyrs'), the subsequent Chalcedonian/non-Chalcedonian split that divided Eastern Christianity, and most recently in modern Egypt — attacks on Coptic churches, homes, and businesses (particularly during the 2011-2013 period of Islamic extremist violence), discrimination in education and employment, and barriers to church construction. Pope Tawadros II leads the church in the contemporary period.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Coptic Orthodox Church — claiming 2000 years of continuous Egyptian Christian tradition, preserving ancient Egyptian language in liturgy, representing the Middle East's largest Christian community — is historically significant as one of Christianity's most ancient traditions and a monument to Christian survival under Islamic majority rule.
